title: Cost Model API Rollout – Risk Assessment & Canary Gating Criteria (SCM v1)
content:
Doc purpose
Assess launch/rollout risk for the Standard Cost Model (SCM) Cost Model API as a dependency of Console cost breakdown pages and Optimize “what-if” sweeps. This doc focuses on: dependency mapping, known failure modes, required client fallbacks, canary gating criteria, and go/no-go checks.

Scope / assumptions
- SCM outputs are NOT billing source-of-truth for invoices in initial release (technical attribution + consistent estimates only).
- Console/Optimize integrations are feature-flagged and can be rolled out by tenant/tier.
- Cost Model service is regional; clients call the nearest region by default via API gateway.
- Determinism requirement: same inputs => same outputs for a given SCM version (see ADR-0147).

Owners / contacts
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (oncall owner), Rafael Mendes (canary/alerting)
- Platform/Service: Priya Natarajan (owner), Jordan Lee (versioning/determinism)
- Console: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin
- Optimize: Hassan Mirza / Yara Haddad
- Telemetry: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman
- Security: Dr. Aisha Rahman / Kevin Osei (audit logging)

1) Dependency mapping (what breaks if SCM breaks)
A. Primary dependencies (hard)
1. Console cost breakdown (interactive UI)
   - Console backend calls Cost Model API to fetch estimate/explain payload
   - UI renders breakdown components + tooltips based on explain fields
   - User impact if degraded: missing breakdown, incorrect “$0” displays, partial or stale results

2. Optimize “what-if” sweeps (batching/caching/quant profile candidates)
   - Optimize calls Cost Model API in bulk to evaluate scenario deltas
   - User impact if degraded: missing recommendations, misleading recommendations if partial results are treated as complete

B. Secondary dependencies (soft/indirect)
3. Internal tooling (ad hoc debugging / support workflows)
   - used for explaining customer discrepancy reports; requires stable explain output

4. Observability / drift detectors
   - mismatch detectors comparing SCM estimates vs metered attribution (where available)
   - if detectors fail silently, we lose early warning for regressions

C. Upstream dependencies (inputs SCM relies on)
- Telemetry pipeline availability and dimensional integrity (region/SKU/quant_profile_id; prefill/decode; batch_size_effective; cache hit metrics)
- Model catalog / metadata resolution (GPU SKU normalization; quant profile metadata)
- AuthN/Z + audit logging pipeline
- API gateway routing + rate limiting

D. Downstream behaviors (what customers see)
- Console: cost breakdown tables, “estimated” labeling, assumptions/confidence messaging
- Optimize: recommendation deltas and confidence; guardrails to suppress output if low confidence / missing critical signals

2) Failure modes (ranked) + mitigations
Legend
- Severity: S0 (worst) -> S3 (minor)
- Likelihood: High/Med/Low based on pre-prod signals and similar launches

2.1 API unavailability (5xx / regional outage / deploy regression)
- Severity: S1 for Console (degraded page), S1-S2 for Optimize (recommendation pipeline impact)
- Likelihood: Med (new service + new traffic patterns)
- Symptoms:
  - Console endpoints timing out -> UI stalls / error states
  - Optimize sweep jobs back up; queue latency increases
- Mitigations:
  - Client timeouts (strict) + retries (bounded) + circuit breaker
  - Console fallback: serve cached last-known-good breakdown (tenant+route+model version keyed) where possible; otherwise display “Breakdown temporarily unavailable” with no numeric substitution (avoid $0)
  - Optimize fallback: treat SCM failure as “no result”; do not infer 0 delta; suppress recommendation unless minimum scenario set completes
  - Regional failover policy (gateway): if primary region fails, optional failover for estimate endpoint ONLY when determinism inputs are fully specified and region/SKU is explicitly part of inputs; otherwise do not failover (avoid cross-region normalization surprises)
  - Rollback plan: feature flag off (Console + Optimize separately)

2.2 Latency regressions (p95/p99) causing cascading timeouts
- Severity: S1 (Console perceived slowness), S1 (Optimize slower sweeps -> stale recs)
- Likelihood: High (explain endpoint payload + metadata lookups; potential cache misses)
- Known contributing factors:
  - Cold caches for model catalog/quant metadata
  - High-cardinality inputs bypassing memoization
  - Audit logging synchronous path (should be async)
- Mitigations:
  - Enforce server-side deadline budgets per request stage (parse/validate, metadata resolve, calc engine)
  - Require internal caching for metadata resolution; pre-warm with top models/regions
  - Console should request estimate (lighter) for list views; only call explain on drill-in (if applicable)
  - Optimize batching: limit scenario count per request; backpressure and queue controls
  - SRE: set alerting on p95 and p99; add automatic “degrade mode” flag recommendation if p99 > threshold (details in gating)

2.3 Input validation mismatches (clients missing required fields / telemetry missing dimensions)
- Severity: S1 (Console shows blank or $0 if mishandled), S2 for Optimize
- Likelihood: Med (integration churn; telemetry gaps)
- Example already seen: validation rejecting missing region -> elevated error rate (see oncall thread + similar to INT-1041 patterns)
- Mitigations:
  - Strict schema contract + client-side pre-validation for required fields
  - Server returns structured error with actionable missing fields; never return partial numeric breakdown as success
  - Console must not coerce failures to 0; must propagate “unavailable” state
  - Telemetry backfill policy: explicit “unknown” values allowed ONLY where spec permits; assumptions/confidence must reflect this

2.4 Determinism / version negotiation bugs (wrong SCM version or silent fallback)
- Severity: S1 (trust/consistency), can be S0 if it corrupts widespread UI trust (“numbers changed without any config change”)
- Likelihood: Med (new negotiation path)
- Failure patterns:
  - Client requests v2, server falls back to v1 but does not clearly indicate
  - Mixed responses across fleet due to partial rollout
- Mitigations:
  - Explicit response headers: scm_version_resolved + negotiation_outcome
  - Compatibility tests in CI (ENG-23203 / PR-18533)
  - Canary must validate consistency: same request repeated N times yields identical output (within exact float formatting rules)
  - Rollout must be atomic per region cluster to avoid mixed negotiation results

2.5 Incorrect cost attribution due to runtime signal bugs (batch_size_effective, prefill/decode split)
- Severity: S0-S1 (incorrect breakdown drives wrong Optimize recs; customer trust loss)
- Likelihood: Med (new runtime instrumentation + known prior bug)
- Known issue: batch_size_effective computed pre-admission control (fixed in PR-18618)
- Mitigations:
  - Canary compares SCM vs metered attribution for fixed prompt sets (perf-canary/pr-421)
  - Mismatch detector dashboards and alert thresholds; disable Optimize consumption on sustained drift
  - Add “confidence: low” when critical signals are missing or marked unstable; Optimize must treat low-confidence as “do not recommend” unless explicitly allowed for internal-only experiments

2.6 Telemetry cardinality blow-up / cost spikes in observability systems
- Severity: S2 (infra cost + dropped metrics leading to blind spots); can become S1 if we lose metering signals at peak
- Likelihood: Med (new dimensions: quant_profile_id, route, model, sku)
- Mitigations:
  - Enforce cardinality controls in telemetry pipeline (PR-18519)
  - Aggregation strategy: cap per-tenant+route breakdown series; sample or bucket long-tail routes
  - SRE monitoring: ingestion rate alarms; dashboards for “dropped labels/series”

2.7 Audit logging overhead / sensitive data exposure
- Severity: S1 for performance; S0 if policy violation (sensitive customer data leaked)
- Likelihood: Low-Med (depends on final event fields and redaction)
- Mitigations:
  - Audit events must be async and non-blocking
  - Strict redaction rules: never log full request payload; log hashes/ids (tenant_id, actor_id, endpoint, scm_version, high-level dimensions)
  - Access controls: limit who can call explain endpoint for customer-specific detail
  - Security sign-off required for GA rollout (ENG-23231 / PR-18579)

3) Required client fallback behaviors (must-haves for launch)
3.1 Console (cost breakdown UI)
- Timeout budget: default 800ms client-side for service call, fail fast; one retry max with jitter for idempotent estimate calls.
- Caching: cache last-known-good by (tenant_id, model_id, route_id, region, scm_version) with short TTL (e.g., 5–15m) and “stale while revalidate” behavior.
- On error/timeout:
  - Never display “$0” or empty components as if valid.
  - Show explicit state: “Breakdown temporarily unavailable” + link to status/help.
  - Keep the overall page usable; avoid blocking unrelated Console sections.
- On low confidence:
  - Display “Estimated (low confidence)” label; surface assumptions summary; hide overly granular breakdown rows if they are derived from missing signals.

3.2 Optimize (what-if sweeps)
- Bulk safety:
  - Enforce max scenarios per sweep request; reject/queue beyond limit.
  - If any scenario fails, treat sweep as partial and do not emit a recommendation unless coverage threshold is met (suggested: >= 90% scenarios succeed AND baseline scenario succeeds).
- Confidence guardrails:
  - Require minimum confidence for a recommendation (threshold defined below).
  - If SCM indicates missing critical signals (e.g., unknown sku, unknown quant profile), mark scenario invalid.
- Retries:
  - Prefer retry at job level, not per-scenario tight loops; avoid thundering herd.

4) Canary gating criteria (go/no-go)
These are the proposed gating checks for each rollout step (staging -> prod canary -> broader prod). The goal is to catch correctness + reliability regressions before expanding blast radius.

4.1 Rollout stages
Stage 0: Staging only
- Console staging + Optimize staging integrated tests (PR-18703)
- Load test harness against staging-like data (PR-18641)

Stage 1: Prod canary (internal tenants only)
- Enable for Redwood internal tenant(s) and 1–3 friendly external tenants (by agreement) for Console breakdown only
- Optimize remains internal-only at first unless SRE signs off

Stage 2: Limited GA (by tier)
- Expand to ~5% tenants by traffic (Hosted) + 1 Dedicated cluster
- Add Optimize for a subset of tenants where we can monitor recommendation drift

Stage 3: Broad GA
- Expand gradually with automated rollback triggers

4.2 Core service SLO gates (must pass for stage progression)
(Exact SLO numbers are referenced in the SLO doc; below are rollout gates for launch, slightly stricter for canary.)
- Availability gate: >= 99.9% success rate for estimate endpoint over 24h canary window (exclude client-canceled)
- Latency gate:
  - estimate p95 <= 150ms; p99 <= 400ms (canary window)
  - explain p95 <= 250ms; p99 <= 700ms (canary window)
- Error budget gate: no SEV2+ incidents attributable to SCM in canary window

4.3 Correctness / drift gates
- Determinism gate: identical request repeated 20x across 2 canary pods yields identical total + breakdown (byte-for-byte JSON for stable key order / canonical float formatting) for same scm_version.
- Metered-vs-estimated drift gate (where metered attribution exists):
  - Median absolute percentage error <= 5% for total
  - p95 absolute percentage error <= 12% for total
  - Any single component (compute/memory/cache) p95 drift <= 20% (component-level can be looser initially)
- Regression gate: no sustained mismatch detector alert firing > 15 minutes in canary window.

4.4 Client impact gates
Console
- Console page-level: no statistically significant increase in “cost page” p95 latency > +150ms attributable to SCM calls
- No increase in Console 5xx rates on cost endpoints
- “Breakdown unavailable” banner rate <= 0.5% of eligible page loads in canary

Optimize
- Job health: sweep completion rate >= 99% for internal test cohort
- Recommendation suppression: if low-confidence or partial, ensure suppression happens (validate via logs + metrics); zero “recommendation emitted with confidence=low” events in canary

4.5 Automatic rollback triggers (during staged rollout)
- SCM service 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5 consecutive minutes (estimate) OR > 1% for 5 minutes (explain)
- p99 latency > 2x gate for 10 minutes
- Mismatch detector critical alert for > 15 minutes
- Console “breakdown unavailable” exceeds 2% for > 10 minutes
Actions:
1) Flip off feature flags for Console client first (reduce user-facing impact)
2) Rate-limit / disable explain endpoint next (keep estimate alive)
3) Roll back last service deploy if correlated
4) Declare incident if customer impact confirmed

5) Known risks / open questions (as of last edit)
1) Explain payload size and cacheability
- Risk: large payloads increase latency and cost; harder to cache.
- Ask: do we need a “thin explain” mode for Console tooltips vs full attribution?

2) Cross-region normalization policy
- Risk: estimates differ if clients omit region/SKU and server infers.
- Proposal: treat region and sku as required for deterministic outputs; if missing, return error with assumptions, not an inferred success.

3) Telemetry freshness / delayed signals
- Risk: attribution/explain may be based on delayed telemetry; user sees inconsistent breakdown.
- Proposal: include “signal_freshness_ms” in explain metadata and surface “data may be delayed” for older-than-threshold.

4) Dedicated/Private deployments
- Risk: different telemetry pipelines / missing dimensions cause systemic low-confidence.
- Proposal: start Hosted first; require explicit readiness checklist per Dedicated cluster and Private environment.

6) Launch readiness checklist (condensed)
- [ ] SLO dashboards live and reviewed (error rate, latency, saturation)
- [ ] Canary comparisons in place (perf-canary) and verified for fixed prompt set
- [ ] Console fallback behavior verified (no $0 display; stale-cache path works)
- [ ] Optimize guardrails verified (no low-confidence recs; partial sweep suppression)
- [ ] Telemetry cardinality control verified post-deploy
- [ ] Audit logging approved by security; redaction verified
- [ ] Feature flags configured for tenant-by-tenant rollout and emergency off switch
- [ ] Oncall runbook updated with top failure modes + rollback steps

Appendix A: Quick mapping of risk -> primary mitigation owners
- Latency regressions: Platform (Priya) + SRE (Sean) + Console (Chloe) timeout/caching
- Validation errors / missing region: Platform (Jordan) + Clients (Chloe/Hassan)
- Signal bugs: Runtime (Mateo/Omar/Sofia) + Applied ML (Arjun) + SRE drift gates
- Cardinality: Telemetry (Logan/Thomas) + SRE monitors
- Audit logging: Security (Aisha/Kevin) + Platform (Felix)

Change log
- 2025-02-18: initial draft (SRE)
- 2025-02-26: added rollback triggers + client impact gates after staging timeouts observed
- 2025-03-04: updated drift thresholds + referenced batch_size_effective prior bug fix; added explicit Console “no $0” requirement
